H4AZ02184.name: Jonathan Nez
H4AZ02184.bio: Former President of the Navajo Nation.

positions.stance: Will fight to lower healthcare costs by taking on "Big Pharma's price gouging," cracking down on surprise medical bills, and reversing Medicaid cuts that threaten rural hospitals.
Wants to prioritize local residents over private equity in single-family home purchases and increase incentives for first-time homebuyers.
Will fight to reverse "crippling and erratic tariff policies," expand rural apprenticeships and workforce training, and streamline small businesses' access to loans and capital.
Wants to help families afford childcare and eldercare through grants, tax credits, and partnerships, and to recruit and retain teachers in rural areas.
Will fight to secure water rights settlements giving Arizona its fair share, invest in rural water infrastructure, and protect groundwater.

H4AZ03109.name: Yassamin Ansari
H4AZ03109.bio: Member of Congress serving on the House Oversight and Natural Resources Committees; began her career as an advisor on the UN Secretary-General's Climate Action Team.

positions.stance: Supports Medicare for All, building more affordable housing, free childcare for working families, and raising the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour.
Believes "we must abolish and prosecute ICE" and supports comprehensive immigration reform protecting Dreamers, refugees, and asylum seekers.
Supports legislation to ban artificial superintelligence, pause advanced AI research, and create a federal agency to regulate the AI industry.
Is "leading the charge to impeach Pete Hegseth" and, on the House Oversight Committee, investigating Jeffrey Epstein's crimes and Trump family corruption.
Takes no corporate PAC money and "supports legislation to Abolish Super PACS to get big money out of politics."

wiki:jacob-parkman.name: Jacob Parkman
wiki:jacob-parkman.bio: Holds a Ph.D. in chemistry and has taught at the high-school, community-college, and university levels.

positions.stance: Wants to "protect religious liberty, constitutional rights, freedom of conscience, limited government, and the rule of law."
Supports locally supported networks that help neighbors meet temporary needs "without creating permanent government dependency," seeded by short-term government grants.
Supports homeschooling and educational choice and wants to integrate high school with community college, expanding certificates, technical training, and degrees.
Wants to increase transparency, competition, direct patient-provider relationships, primary-care access, and telehealth while lowering administrative costs.
Would protect current beneficiaries while developing a sustainable system giving future generations "greater ownership, investment choice, and retirement assets."

H8AZ09040.name: Greg Stanton
H8AZ09040.bio: Member of Congress for Arizona's 4th District and former Mayor of Phoenix.

positions.stance: Will not accept a Colorado River agreement that lets other Basin states avoid their fair share, and pushes funding for water recycling, groundwater recharge, and drought resilience.
Calls lowering living costs his "top priority," backing rolling back Trump's tariffs, restarting the Affordable Connectivity Program, and raising the minimum wage.

Believes reproductive decisions "belong to women, in consultation with their doctors and families, not politicians"; supports restoring federal abortion protections and defending contraception and IVF.
Supports banning congressional stock trading, enforceable Supreme Court ethics rules, stronger whistleblower protections, and refusing ICE more funding until it is overhauled.
Pushing to pass the PRO Act, raise the minimum wage, expand paid sick leave, invest in "CHIPS 2.0," and expand job training and apprenticeships.

H4AZ04115.name: Zuhdi Jasser
H4AZ04115.bio: Primary-care physician and small business owner for over two decades, retired U.S. Navy lieutenant commander, and founder of the American Islamic Forum for Democracy.

positions.stance: Wants to rein in wasteful spending, let Americans keep more of their earnings, cut needless regulations, bring manufacturing home, and "curb foreign investors pricing out families."
Supports "a Balanced Budget Amendment to the United States Constitution" and pledges to fight to get federal spending under control.
Will support more resources for border agents and prioritize border security, saying "people should knock on your door before they come in."
Supports "educational freedom" and "funding students — not systems," backing policies that empower parents.
Says "we need to stop subsidizing our ailments and start solving them," pledging to put Americans' health and freedoms ahead of special interests.

H6AZ05265.name: Mark Lamb
H6AZ05265.bio: Retired sheriff who served eight years as Sheriff of Pinal County, Arizona, after working as a police officer and detective.

positions.stance: Pledges to "support law enforcement" in Congress, drawing on eight years as sheriff confronting cartels and human trafficking.
Wants to "stop the cartels, enforce the law, and protect legal immigration and commerce," securing the border and restoring order to the immigration system.
Wants to "lower costs, support small businesses, protect taxpayers, and strengthen American jobs."

H6AZ05240.name: Elizabeth Lee
H6AZ05240.bio: Registered nurse and board-certified patient advocate who has worked in reproductive healthcare and fertility clinics for over a decade.

positions.stance: Would cosponsor and fight to pass Medicare for All and expand Medicare to include mental health, dental, vision, and hearing coverage.
Would "crack down on corporate landlords and investment firms buying up single-family homes" and provide first-time homebuyer and down payment assistance.
Wants to close tax loopholes for billionaires and corporations and "ensure no billionaire pays a lower tax rate than a nurse or teacher."
Would increase federal education funding to close gaps between districts, raise teacher salaries toward a national minimum, and reduce class sizes.
Would support legislation "like the Equality Act to protect against discrimination in healthcare, housing, employment, education, and public life."

H2AZ02360.name: Juan Ciscomani
H2AZ02360.bio: Member of Congress for Arizona's 6th District, serving on the Appropriations and Veterans' Affairs committees.

positions.stance: Has worked to expand veterans' homeownership opportunities and education benefits and to ensure surviving families receive their promised benefits.
Supports tax relief to help Arizonans "keep more of what they earn," including eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security.
Seeks federal dollars for local infrastructure, public safety, transportation, airport, bridge, and water projects across Southern Arizona.
Advocated for a new military mission for Fort Huachuca to protect jobs and strengthen national security.
Focuses on expanding rural health care access, funding cancer and medical research, and rooting out "waste, fraud, and abuse" in health spending.

H6AZ06099.name: JoAnna Mendoza
H6AZ06099.bio: Retired U.S. Marine who served 20 years in uniform.

positions.stance: Would crack down on price gouging, modernize the Child Tax Credit, oppose "reckless tariffs," and oppose any efforts to cut Social Security benefits.
Supports workforce training, apprenticeships, and technical education, small businesses, and "the right to unionize."
Would reverse cuts to AHCCCS and enhanced ACA subsidies, expand Medicare drug price negotiation, and opposes privatizing Medicare.
Supports law enforcement funding, stronger security at ports of entry, deporting violent criminals, and legal pathways to citizenship for people who work hard and follow the law.
Supports American-made and clean energy investment, requiring data centers to "bring their own energy," securing Arizona's Colorado River share, and a five-year Farm Bill.

H6AZ07121.name: Adelita Grijalva
H6AZ07121.bio: Former Chair of the Pima County Board of Supervisors and former Tucson Unified School District Governing Board member who worked at Pima County Teen Court for more than 25 years.

positions.stance: Supports comprehensive immigration reform with a pathway to legalization, protections for DACA recipients, ending mandatory and family detention, and phasing out private detention facilities.
Opposes "harmful tariffs," supports the Raise the Wage Act's $17 minimum wage, a larger Earned Income and Child Tax Credit, and the PRO Act.
Supports investment in solar, wind, and battery projects, clean-energy incentives for households, and modernizing the 1872 Mining Law to require royalties on public-land minerals.
Opposes proposals placing "the vast majority of long-term water cuts on Arizona" and pledges to protect Tribal water settlements and Yuma County agriculture.
Supports protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act, restoring federal Medicaid funding, lowering prescription drug costs, and access to medication abortion and contraceptives.

H4AZ07134.name: Daniel Butierez
H4AZ07134.bio: Small business owner who runs two businesses.

positions.stance: Wants to "secure the Southern Border and fight to give U.S. Border Patrol the resources they need to do their job."
Will "fight to cut taxes and make the tax code simpler for small businesses."
Wants to promote job growth and economic development "by enabling responsible mining practices in Southern Arizona."

H4AZ08108.name: Abraham Hamadeh
H4AZ08108.bio: Member of Congress and military veteran.

positions.stance: Says "Border Security is National Security" and pledges to allocate resources to end illegal border crossings and always vote to defend the border.
Will work to ensure voting rolls are clean and that "ranked choice voting is banned at the federal level."
Says the federal government must return to passing a budget and "have the courage to live within our means and stop bankrupting future generations."
Wants fentanyl reclassified as a "dangerous" drug or "poison" in the criminal code to allow harsher punishment and enhanced sentencing.
Will "continue to support funding, backing, and revitalizing police forces across the country" and enforce existing laws.

H4AZ08082.name: Bernadette Greene-Placentia
H4AZ08082.bio: Long-haul trucker for 27 years and owner of a small trucking business.

positions.stance: Supports lowering the cost of groceries, fuel, and energy, expanding affordable housing, and fighting inflation with "practical, fiscally responsible solutions."
Would protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts, "require very high earners to contribute more fairly to Social Security," and force drug price renegotiation.
Would protect coverage for pre-existing conditions, require clear prices before patients are billed, and "gradually lower the age of medicare eligibility."
Would reduce VA wait times, expand mental-health services, and preserve community-care options when the VA cannot provide timely care.
Supports strong border security with modern technology and staffing, and "an earned pathway to citizenship for law-abiding immigrants who contribute to our communities."

H0AZ01259.name: Paul Gosar
H0AZ01259.bio: Member of Congress and former Chairman of the Congressional Western Caucus and of the House Subcommittee on Minerals and Energy.

positions.stance: Fighting to "eliminate all taxes on Social Security Benefits" and eliminate pension and income offsets so retirees collect 100% of their benefits.
Calls the right to keep and bear arms "absolute" and opposes a national gun registry and other legislation that erodes gun rights.
Will "continue to support true spending cuts and a Balanced Budget Amendment to the Constitution."
Supports U.S. energy independence and opening federal lands in Arizona to "reasonable usages for agriculture and natural resource development."
Supports President Trump's border wall and opposes amnesty efforts.

H6AZ09085.name: Danielle Sterbinsky
H6AZ09085.bio: U.S. Navy veteran and certified human resources professional with a master's degree in industrial-organizational psychology.

positions.stance: Pledges to "put country before party" and to protect free and fair elections, constitutional checks and balances, and ethical government.
Supports strong transition support to civilian careers, accessible healthcare and mental health services, and stability for military families.
Supports long-term water protection and investing in a diverse energy mix, "including traditional energy and renewable sources," while keeping energy reliable and affordable.
Supports fixed-income protections, affordable healthcare and housing, inflation relief, and eliminating the Social Security tax cap.
Wants to expedite the legal immigration process, "strengthen border security and enforce the law responsibly," and pursue humane, practical solutions.

H8MA02041.name: Richard Neal
H8MA02041.bio: Congressman for Western and Central Massachusetts and former Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee.

positions.stance: Prioritizes "regional equity" and the region's fair share of federal funding, and champions improving and expanding passenger rail between Pittsfield, Springfield, Worcester, and Boston.
Calls climate change "a profound threat" and says sustainability must be part of every policy area, from trade to infrastructure to health care.
Supports a new assault weapons ban, universal background checks, a bump stock ban, and a minimum age of 21 to buy all firearms.
Working to cover more people and make coverage more affordable, and supports Medicare negotiating lower drug prices.
Supports comprehensive immigration reform, a pathway to citizenship for DREAMers, birthright citizenship, and expediting work visas.

H4MA03022.name: Jim McGovern
H4MA03022.bio: Congressman for Massachusetts' 2nd District since 1996; former senior aide to U.S. Representative Joe Moakley.

positions.stance: Has authored legislation to increase Pell Grant funding so more students can access higher education.
Describes himself as "a strong proponent of healthcare reform," including reducing the cost of home health care.
Works to end hunger at home and abroad, including expanding the McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Program.
Fighting "to overturn Citizens United" and against corporate personhood.

H8MA03106.name: Lori Trahan
H8MA03106.bio: Congresswoman for Massachusetts' 3rd District; former chief of staff to Congressman Marty Meehan, tech executive, and co-founder of a consulting firm.

positions.stance: Wants to make higher education accessible and affordable, expand targeted aid for students, and hold private universities with high loan default rates accountable.
Says "wealthy families shouldn't pay a lower tax rate than hardworking middle-class families" and wants public funding for infrastructure that creates jobs.
Says "healthcare is a right, not a privilege"; will defend and expand the Affordable Care Act and reduce prescription drug costs.
Supports paid, gender-neutral family leave, closing the pay gap through pay transparency, raising the minimum wage, and the Paycheck Fairness Act.
Supports a pathway to citizenship, bipartisan reform for DACA recipients and DREAMers, more immigration judges, and securing the border "without a wall."

H6MA03100.name: Gary Grossi
H6MA03100.bio: Retired U.S. Army colonel with 29 years of service and a nurse.

positions.stance: Will push for "affordable, evidence-based energy solutions" to lower energy and heating bills immediately.
Wants to "stop unrealistic regulations that drive up housing costs and limit supply" and make homeownership achievable.
Says bureaucracy and inflated malpractice costs are siphoning health care dollars and will fight to "streamline the system and put patients first."
Supports law enforcement with community partnerships that build trust and improve public safety outcomes.
Supports small business growth through Economic Opportunity Zones that create jobs and strengthen local economies.

H0MA04192.name: Jake Auchincloss
H0MA04192.bio: Congressman and former U.S. Marine who commanded infantry in Afghanistan.

positions.stance: Wants to treat "cost disease" in housing, healthcare, and utilities by cutting regulations like bans on starter homes and taking on special interests.
Calls Social Security "sacrosanct" and says the fix should include the wealthiest paying more into the Trust Fund and raising the minimum wage.
Wants to lower deficits through growth, closing tax preferences like the "Buy-Borrow-Die loophole for billionaires," and efficiencies in healthcare delivery.
Leading legislation to raise the minimum age for social media accounts from 13 to 16 and hold social media and AI companies liable for deepfakes and harassment.
Wants low or no co-pays, limits on insurers' abuse of prior authorization, and to defend the integrity of the NIH and FDA.

H6MA04140.name: Tom Stalcup
H6MA04140.bio: Physicist and president of an electronics company that makes environmental monitoring systems.

positions.stance: Calls for "immediate, broad drug price negotiation—without artificial limits on which drugs are included" and allowing safe, equivalent generics to enter the market.
Wants the strongest defense in the world while treating war as "a last resort," and limiting those with financial interests in war to advisory roles.
Wants to restore competition by opening markets to lower-cost alternatives, removing barriers to entry, and enforcing antitrust laws to bring down costs.
Says "parents must have the final say" in how children are taught, and supports more recess and less focus on standardized testing.
Says "human-induced climate change is real and measurable" and supports evidence-based solutions and technologies that do not undermine economic stability.

H4MA05084.name: Katherine Clark
H4MA05084.bio: Congresswoman for Massachusetts' 5th District and, per her site, the highest-ranking woman in Congress.

positions.stance: Believes "every worker should be paid a living wage," with paid family leave and the right to join a union; has fought to lift Trump's tariffs.
Says access to health care "should be a right, not a privilege"; opposes Medicaid cuts and supports extending Affordable Care Act tax credits.
Says it is "past time" to treat child care as "the essential infrastructure that it is."
Supports federal abortion access, protecting birth control access, equal pay for equal work, paid leave, and affordable childcare.
Supports investing in clean energy, centering environmental justice, and shifting recycling costs off consumers and municipalities onto corporate polluters.

H6MA06202.name: Micah Jones
H6MA06202.bio: Attorney and U.S. Army veteran who served as a captain, including a deployment to Afghanistan.

positions.stance: Would "ban the trading of individual stocks by members of Congress and their spouses" and make financial disclosures simple, searchable, and public.
Would advocate federal resources to expand LNG infrastructure to New England, modernize nuclear permitting, and expand renewables without pushing costs onto households.
Wants smarter regulations and less duplicative federal review, saying it is "too difficult, slow, and expensive to build" housing, infrastructure, and businesses.
Supports stronger border enforcement with better staffing and technology, modernizing legal immigration to reduce backlogs, and more judges for timely immigration cases.
Supports law enforcement training, recruitment, and retention, plus targeted violence prevention and coordinated mental health response systems.

H8MA03072.name: Dan Koh
H8MA03072.bio: Former Chief of Staff to the U.S. Department of Labor and to Boston Mayor Marty Walsh, former White House official, and former technology company COO.

positions.stance: Calls Trump "the most corrupt politician this country has ever seen" and pledges to fight back against the administration from Day One.
Refuses corporate PAC money, would vote to overturn Citizens United and ban congressional stock trading, and supports the Freedom to Vote Act.
Supports a comprehensive immigration overhaul, hiring immigration judges and asylum officers to process claims humanely, and expanding new avenues for legal immigration.
Plan sets goals of "no more than $10 a day for childcare," no more than 30% of income on rent, and ending child poverty.
Says "Democrats must take back the White House in 2028" and must take the fight to MAGA directly with fact-based arguments.

H8MA07032.name: Ayanna Pressley
H8MA07032.bio: Congresswoman for Massachusetts' 7th District since 2018 and former at-large Boston City Councilor.

positions.stance: Introduced Federal Job Guarantee legislation to provide public jobs for all adults seeking employment, and has pressed to expand the Child Tax Credit.
Says "abortion care is healthcare and an essential human right" and has co-led legislation to protect and restore abortion access nationwide.
Advocated for the Equality Act and protections for transgender neighbors, and has pressed for federal action against violent white supremacy.
Supports competitive wages for public school teachers, expanded access to higher education, and student debt cancellation.
Wants foreign policy grounded in equity and justice that prioritizes coalition-building and "considers military action to be an absolute last resort."

H2MA09072.name: Stephen Lynch
H2MA09072.bio: U.S. Congressman, attorney, former labor leader, and structural ironworker for nearly 20 years.

positions.stance: Says "there is no question climate change is real" and treats it as an economic and national security issue, supporting fuel efficiency and renewable fuels.
Opposes unfair trade deals and supports equal pay, paid leave, a higher minimum wage, and ensuring the wealthiest and largest corporations "pay their fair share."
Supports universal background checks for all firearm purchases, barring people on the No-Fly list from buying guns, and federal support for state "red flag" laws.
Co-sponsors the Equality Act and George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and supports the Equal Rights Amendment and Paycheck Fairness Act.
Conducts oversight of military operations, supports troops exposed to toxic hazards, and introduced legislation to ban deep fake audio, video, and photos in U.S. elections.

H0MA10082.name: Bill Keating
H0MA10082.bio: Congressman for Massachusetts' 9th District since 2011 and former Norfolk District Attorney and state legislator.

positions.stance: Is "challenging Trump's tariffs, which increase prices on everyday goods and harm small businesses," and focuses on practical solutions to lower costs.
Advocates for "more affordable and accessible healthcare for everyone."
Has fought to protect Social Security and Medicare.
Has fought to defend reproductive rights.
Has fought to support veterans and military families.

H6MA09206.name: Tyler MacAllister
H6MA09206.bio: Five-term member of the Mattapoisett Select Board.

positions.stance: Will "take on the mandates and Washington spending driving up kitchen-table costs" and fight for policy that rewards work.
Backs "an all-of-the-above energy approach that puts reliable, affordable power ahead of ideology" to bring energy costs down.
Will fight to cut federal waste, hold Washington accountable for every dollar, and bring tax dollars back to the district.
Will oppose "federal overreach and bad rules choking the fleet" and push for practical, science-based fishing policy.
Will fight to keep the region's coastline, harbors, small businesses, and traditions "in local hands."

H0TN01118.name: Diana Harshbarger
H0TN01118.bio: Member of Congress and community pharmacist for over 30 years.

positions.stance: Committed to reinstating Trump-era immigration policies, including "completing the border wall, defunding 'sanctuary' cities, ending 'catch and release.'"
Calls herself "a staunch defender of your 2nd Amendment rights" and will oppose attempts to restrict law-abiding citizens' right to bear arms.
Dedicated to passing legislation that "imposes term limits on all federal offices."
Advocates tackling illegal drugs at the border, increasing funding for rehabilitation, and holding those who created the crisis accountable.
Will champion "America First policies" and provide the military with the tools and resources to counter threats from Russia, China, and Iran.
